_convention: Every fix of a real defect (security/correctness/crash/leak/race/injection/data-loss) gets an entry IN THE SAME COMMIT that fixes it. A review flagging already-fixed code is recorded as status='verified-stale', never re-fixed (G1/G11). Hygiene/refactor items are NOT remediations. Re-run index_file on this JSON after edits.

entries.finding: CLR-W2-FDLEAK (bug review 2026-09-25 @ sha 8afa3ca9, CONFIRMED, still open on 2026-09-26 bytes): load_spec opened the spec source with a bare `open(source, encoding="utf-8-sig", errors="ignore").read()` and never closed the handle - repeated spec loads in batch use exhaust file descriptors.
entries.fix: `with open(...) as f: raw = f.read()` - deterministic close on every path including read failure (exception still propagates; the with-block only guarantees close, never swallows).

entries.finding: CLR-W2-SOCKLEAK (bug review 2026-09-25 @ sha 8afa3ca9, CONFIRMED): `json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20))` never closed the HTTP response; mitigated in practice by _MODEL_MAX_CACHE (one call per model per process) but still one leaked socket per uncached model, and the except-path leaves nothing to collect. Sibling precedent done right: app.py:21 `with urllib.request.urlopen(...) as r:`.
entries.fix: `with _u.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as resp:` wrapping the model scan loop - response closed on success, on no-match, and on any parse/transport exception before the except guard.

entries.finding: CLR-W2-AUTO-DIVERGENCE (NEW, perfection L2 pass A 2026-09-26 @ sha 8afa3ca9): the :317 comment documented max_tokens AUTO as `None/<=0` but the code `int(_mt) if _mt` only mapped None/0 to the model ceiling; a negative value - reachable via `run_batch --max-tokens -5` (argparse type=int, no floor) - was sent to the API and failed 400 per file instead of using the ceiling, violating the file's own documented contract.
entries.fix: `max_tokens = int(_mt) if (_mt or 0) > 0 else model_max_tokens(...)` - the comment's None/<=0 contract is now literally the predicate; input partition {None, 0, -5} -> ceiling, {5000} -> 5000.

entries.finding: CLR-W3-MODECOERCE (quality review 2026-09-26 @ 8afa3ca9): an unknown `mode` was silently coerced to "bug" - a caller typo (e.g. "quaity") produced a billed bug review with no signal. MODES is the product's whole mode vocabulary; the gate is this file's to enforce. Caller audit: app.py builds modes from constants, run_batch restricts via argparse choices, legacy drivers pass literals - no live caller can send an invalid mode, so raising is safe today and typo-proof tomorrow.
entries.fix: Loud ValueError before any spend: `raise ValueError("unknown mode %r; expected one of %s" % (mode, sorted(MODES)))` replacing the coercion - message names the bad value and the full valid set; raised above the key check so no client is ever constructed.

entries.finding: CLR-W4-NORETRY (quality review 2026-09-26 @ 8afa3ca9): a single transient API error (429/5xx/connection blip) mid-batch marked the file errored - run_batch records status:error, spend on prior files stands, and a re-run re-pays input tokens for the whole file set unless shas changed. Direct cost consequence for a tool whose premise is cheap triage.
entries.fix: Bounded transient retry: _transient() recognizes RateLimitError(429)/APIStatusError>=500/APIConnectionError/APITimeoutError (verified against installed openai 3.19.2); _call_retry() wraps BOTH the primary call and the corrective JSON-retry call - after a failed attempt a it sleeps retry_backoff_base * 2**(a-1) (defaults 3 attempts / 1.0s base = 3.0s worst added wall time), re-raises non-transient errors at once, propagates the last transient exception when the budget is exhausted. Knobs are cfg-driven per the file's constitution (retry_max_attempts=1 disables).
entries.verification: RED-first: 7 checks failed on pre-fix bytes (ratelimit/5xx/conn recovery, usage-from-success-only, exhaustion-raises-last, backoff shape, JSON-retry composition). entries.finding: CLR-W7-STAGEE-BLIND (hy4-preview Stage-E blind review @ 8813baf2... sha 8818baf2, CONFIRMED by Phase-3): (1) the OpenAI client constructed per review_code call was never closed - pool ownership left to GC timing (SDK __enter__/__exit__/close verified on openai 3.19.2); (2) _MODEL_MAX_CACHE keyed by model only while lookups take base_url - the file's live-per-call api_base means switching providers in one process served the wrong ceiling for the same model id; (3) load_spec compared raw registry id values against the string ids filter, so numeric-id registries never matched and spec mode raised 'no matching spec rows' for rows that exist. None of the three were in the local record - the author-blind-spot residue the protocol's external stage exists to catch.

entries.finding: Do not cache refusals or incomplete responses as completed reviews: process unconditionally saves analyzer output. Missing keys/specs return refusal text at zero cost; token exhaustion can return only a diagnostic. save_review stores only the SHA, so status marks these reviewed and hides them from outstanding work. run_batch.py:152-160 has the same incomplete-response path.
entries.fix: Require explicit complete response status from analyzer; incomplete/refused/truncated/invalid responses retain evidence and cost but no completed-cache credit. Failed retries preserve prior completed reviews, immutable bodies and total attempt cost. Exports and console label completed modes separately. Contradictory finish fields, empty or nonstring replies cannot earn new credit. Legacy canonical records without completion flags retain historical status for compatibility. This fixes the new-write defect; it does not certify old unmarked records. Existing unmarked responses cannot reliably prove completion from text alone; users can force a fresh review to replace them. No historical completion backfill is claimed.
